'''''Aristida adscensionis''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common name '''sixweeks threeawn'''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Murthy |first1=M. Sreedhara |last2=Nagodra |first2=Taruna |date=1977 |title=Allelopathic Effects of Aristida adscensionis on Rhizobium |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2401843 |journal=Journal of Applied Ecology |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=279–282 |doi=10.2307/2401843 |jstor=2401843 |bibcode=1977JApEc..14..279M |issn=0021-8901|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It is native to the Americas but it is distributed nearly worldwide. It grows easily in disturbed and waste areas and has potential to become a weed.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fatima |first1=Sana |last2=Hameed |first2=Mansoor |last3=Ahmad |first3=Farooq |last4=Ashraf |first4=Muhammad |last5=Ahmad |first5=Rashid |date=2018-12-01 |title=Structural and functional modifications in a typical arid zone species Aristida adscensionis L. along altitudinal gradient |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0367253018301592 |journal=Flora |language=en |volume=249 |pages=172–182 |doi=10.1016/j.flora.2018.11.003 |bibcode=2018FMDFE.249..172F |issn=0367-2530|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Description==
This annual [[bunchgrass]] is quite variable in appearance, its size and shape determined largely by environmental conditions. It grows in a tuft to heights between 5 and 80 centimeters. It forms a narrow [[inflorescence]] of spikelets, each fruit with three [[awn (botany)|awns]].
